name: Charge Robotics Sunrise
specialisedFor: utility-scale solar construction: assembling tracker bays (torque tubes, brackets, modules) and installing them on the piles
summary: A portable robotic factory set up on a utility-scale solar site that assembles torque tubes, brackets and PV modules into complete tracker bays and delivers them for installation on the piles, run by the maker's own crew.

germany.statusNote: Not sold as a machine: Charge offers Sunrise as a turnkey service with its own trained crew on US utility-scale solar sites (HQ San Leandro, California; field jobs based in Phoenix, Arizona). No European offer, partner or project found.

specs.label: Bay delivered as one unit
specs.conditions: MIT News (2025): each bay a 40-foot section weighing about 800 pounds

notes: A sheltered assembly line on the site, not a single mobile robot; robotic arms handle all component movement (number of arms not stated; set to 2 as the source speaks of arms in the plural).

Wheeled delivery vehicles take finished bays to the piles; MIT News (2025) describes an autonomous robotic vehicle, while a current maker photo shows the bay carrier pulled by a tractor with a driver.
Automates all mechanical installation except pile driving; civil works and electrical work stay with the EPC.
Machine vision checks part placement before fastening; every fastening is logged with torque, serial number, time and image.
Can run 24/7; operators run the robotic equipment remotely (CEO, MIT News 2025).

images.alt: Charge Robotics Sunrise assembly line set up on a desert solar construction site

evidence.task: Prototype assembled solar bays with computer-vision quality control and installed them in the field
evidence.where: SOLV Energy solar project, USA (site not named)
evidence.note: MIT News (2025) says the prototype built a solar farm with SOLV Energy in early 2024.

evidence.task: First commercial system shipped; the maker is scaling up operations
evidence.note: Maker statement in a job posting; another posting describes running the factory and a fleet of delivery vehicles on solar construction sites across the US.
